Subject: Pilot latency/profile and hosting recommendation (clarify next steps)

Hi Simon / Meera —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap of what I captured and a proposed set of next steps so we can land on whether to start on Hosted API pilot or scope Dedicated capacity up front.

What we heard from MediCart (please flag if I missed anything):
- Primary real-time feature: personalized product recommendations in checkout flow (99% of requests are < 2s tolerance at user-visible layer).
- Typical steady traffic: ~300 qps; expected peak / marketing bursts: ~1,500 qps for 2–15 minute windows.
- Latency goals: median <= 40 ms token time (end-to-end response target ~250 ms for 100-token responses), 95th <= 120 ms for model inference portion.
- Data: no special compliance constraints right now — may revisit for PHI if pilot expands.

Redwood's quick read: the traffic profile (high short bursts) and tight tail-latency target mean we should validate batching and KV/cache behavior. Hosted API can run a short pilot to prove latency/quality quickly; Dedicated capacity becomes attractive once you need predictable tail latency and committed throughput for bursts. Private VPC/on-prem not required for initial pilot based on current compliance notes.

Proposed next steps (simple, 2-week cadence):
1) Pilot on Hosted API (2 weeks): Redwood runs a controlled pilot that mirrors your peak burst using your sample prompts and a synthetic arrival pattern. Deliverables: latency/95th percentile report, token cost estimate, and a suggested Dedicated config if needed.
2) Parallel estimates: Redwood will provide a Dedicated capacity cost/throughput estimate and an ops runbook for burst handling (autoscaling and pre-warming).
3) Decide: if pilot shows hosted meets 95th target in your burst windows, proceed Hosted for initial rollout; otherwise, schedule a Dedicated evaluation.

Can you share the sample prompt archive and a 48-72 hour qps histogram from your traffic logs? I attached a placeholder for how we prefer the CSV (medicart-qps-profile.csv) — feel free to send as-is.

If that plan looks good I’ll kick off the pilot scope doc and loop in karthik for an infra tuning checklist.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Thanks Neha — this matches my notes. A couple of clarifications from our side:
1) Burst windows are often traffic-driven by push notifications; we can reproduce them on staging.
2) We need to keep the end-to-end impact under 300 ms for the recommendation path. If model inference adds >120 ms tail we start seeing cart abandonment.

I’ll drop the qps histogram and sample prompts by tomorrow EOD. For the Dedicated estimate: can you include a 99th percentile cost/latency trade-off (i.e., a config that favors tail vs one that favors unit cost)?

Also looping in Meera (ops) for any infra questions.

Simon

Hi all — quick technical note after spot-checking the sample prompt shapes you shared (thanks Simon):

Observations (preliminary):
- Median token lengths are low (~40–60 tokens), which is good for batching efficiency in Hosted.
- Burst arrival rates are spiky; to hit a 95th <= 120 ms inference portion reliably you will likely need warm GPU-backed pools with aggressive pre-warm / pinned workers during marketing pushes.

Recommendation matrix (simple):
- Pilot (Hosted): run as-is with orchestration that simulates your burst windows. Focus tests on 95th/99th tail and cold-start behavior. Use prefix/KV cache for repeated user contexts to reduce token compute.
- If pilot shows 95th violations during bursts: Dedicated with reserved GPU pool + pre-warm strategy (single-tenant slices) will reduce tail variability. We’ll include two Dedicated sizing options: (A) cost-optimized (more batching, slightly higher tail) and (B) tail-optimized (extra reserved capacity, lower tail).
- Private VPC: only necessary if you confirm egress/network policy or compliance needs; not required for this initial phase.

Next technical asks for a validated pilot:
- A reproducible burst script (we can provide one) and a representative payload set (you already sent sample prompts).
- A target TPS arrival pattern for the worst 5-minute window.

I’ll attach an internal checklist when we send the Dedicated estimates. Happy to hop on a short call if you want to review the Dedicated sizing tradeoffs before the pilot.

—Karthik
Lead, Inference Optimization, Redwood Inference
